title.narrative: The Project for the Improvement of the Living Conditions in the Informal Settlements in Aleppo and Homs

description.narrative:
The primary specific objective of this project is to improve living conditions of inhabitants and returnees in informal settlements in Aleppo and Homs by upgrading the areas for Sustainable City Early Recovery and Social Cohesion. This will be achieved by upgrading physical infrastructure and status of tenure security in informal settlements.
The overarching objective of this intervention is to lead a pathway for the formal recognition and granting of living rights to vulnerable residents in informal areas. Achieving this goal involves a complex and multifaceted process that encompasses legal, social, economic, and infrastructural aspects. To initiate this process, the two-year project will focus on several key activities, including the preparation of neighborhood profiles, the development of a recovery plan, addressing HLP rights, and implementing physical infrastructure upgrades. These interventions will pave the way for the eventual formalization of informal settlements, thereby granting official recognition and securing residing rights for individuals living in informal settlements over the long term.
This transformation will also empower vulnerable populations to actively contribute to the overall welfare and early recovery of cities. The upgrading informal settlement will enhance the living conditions, stabilize society, and contribute to the peace process (triple nexus), all of which provide a basis for the returning of displaced population.
The improvement of the life of people in informal areas is a crucial step towards sustainable city early recovery, especially for the area where has been deteriorated by the conflict and the recent earthquake. It aligns with broader goals of stability and resilience while accommodating the potential return of displaced populations. Considering this project is showcasing the possible approach for upgrading the informal settlements, this upgrading initiative will create a safe entry point and contribute to further engagement of local stakeholders in adopting innovative urban solutions and procedures.
This project aims to initiate the process of official recognition and granting of residing rights to individuals living in informal areas by supporting upgrading the selected informal settlements in two cities. The formalization of informal settlements requires a collaborative effort involving government agencies, non-governmental organizations, community members, and other stakeholders. In general, the formalization process will involve the extensive surveys, establishing the tenure rights, participatory planning and urban planning solutions, upgrading of infrastructure, housing and social services, economic development, legal reforms to address the regulatory barriers, and etc. However, it is crucial to address the unique challenges of each settlement and tailor solutions to the specific context of the community.
Among them, House and Land Property (HLP) right is one of the key aspects when it comes to the settlements in informal area. In the past seven years UN-Habitat has been working extensively on analyzing the legal and institutional framework in urban areas and voluminous research has been made in the context of an HLP (supported by the EU DG NEAR) and a wealth of recommendations have been issued in fields such as urban land development, local governance, informality, land administration, land economies and others.
UN-Habitat has developed an integrated Urban Recovery Framework for Syria that applied an evidence-based approach, identified through participatory local recovery planning, that analyzes and prioritizes urban needs through multi-dimensional urban information analysis. The Upgrading process in this project will seek to develop a coordinated approach, stemming from knowledge framework (Documentation, Damage assessment, Survey, developing Geographic Information System (GIS) platform, supported by an engagement in informal settlement sensitive topics tenure and Unexploded Ordnance (UXO), integrating social cohesion and resilience in urban planning, capacity building and piloting a number of tailored interventions.
This project is designed based on the previous studies as well as on the research and response by UN-Habitat and other UN agencies to which the Government of Japan has provided significant support after the 2023 earthquake. The 2023 earthquake posed new and significant changes to the HLP landscape in Syria.
Given the sensitivities of this subject, UN-Habitat will carry out a careful context and risk analysis in implementing the project. The stakeholders, their needs, their expectations, as well as potential positive and negative consequence of project intervention will be analysed at the beginning of the project. This step is considered essential for UN-Habitat to identify the challenges clearly to upgrade the informal area, and tailor its process specifically.
